nodes.html: An SMSF can invest in residential or commercial property, but doing so requires a Limited Recourse Borrowing Arrangement (LRBA), a bare trust, a compliant trust deed, and careful contribution management. The fund must remain solely for retirement purposes, and any use of the property must satisfy the 'sole purpose test'. A specialist structures these correctly from day one — getting it wrong can breach SIS Act rules and trigger penalties.

nodes.html: Recent LRBA rule changes for residential property
nodes.text: Recent LRBA rule changes for residential property

nodes.html: Under the Treasury Laws Amendment (Tax Reform No. 1) Act 2026 (effective 10 August 2026), SMSFs are no longer permitted to enter into new Limited Recourse Borrowing Arrangements (LRBAs) to purchase residential property. LRBAs can now only be used to acquire business real property, unless the property is used 100% wholly and exclusively in one or more businesses — for example, a converted residential premises operating strictly as a dental surgery, medical clinic, or allied health practice. Existing residential LRBAs established before 10 August 2026, and contracts exchanged before that date, remain protected under grandfathering rules. Our matched specialists can review whether your proposed purchase qualifies under the new rules.

nodes.html: Holding your business premises inside your SMSF (a 'business real property' arrangement) can be powerful — but the rent must be at market rate, the lease must be properly documented, and related-party rules apply. Our matched specialists structure these arrangements to pass audit scrutiny and keep the fund compliant.

nodes.q: Can my SMSF buy a residential property to rent?
nodes.a: Yes, an SMSF can invest in residential property, but it cannot be lived in by you or any related party. It must be held at arm's length, rented to an unrelated tenant at market rate, and any borrowing must use an LRBA with a bare-trust structure. A specialist structures this correctly — the rules are unforgiving if breached.
nodes.aText: Yes, an SMSF can invest in residential property, but it cannot be lived in by you or any related party. It must be held at arm's length, rented to an unrelated tenant at market rate, and any borrowing must use an LRBA with a bare-trust structure. A specialist structures this correctly — the rules are unforgiving if breached.

nodes.q: Can my SMSF buy my business premises?
nodes.a: Yes — an SMSF can acquire business real property and lease it to your business, provided the rent is at market rate and the lease is properly documented. This is a common strategy, but the documentation and audit trail matter. Our matched specialists handle the structuring and documentation.
nodes.aText: Yes — an SMSF can acquire business real property and lease it to your business, provided the rent is at market rate and the lease is properly documented. This is a common strategy, but the documentation and audit trail matter. Our matched specialists handle the structuring and documentation.

nodes.q: Are there restrictions on SMSF borrowing for property?
nodes.a: Yes. Borrowing inside an SMSF must use a Limited Recourse Borrowing Arrangement (LRBA), which restricts the lender's recourse to the single asset acquired. The asset must be held in a separate bare trust, and the fund's other assets are protected. The matched specialist structures the LRBA correctly from the outset.
nodes.aText: Yes. Borrowing inside an SMSF must use a Limited Recourse Borrowing Arrangement (LRBA), which restricts the lender's recourse to the single asset acquired. The asset must be held in a separate bare trust, and the fund's other assets are protected. The matched specialist structures the LRBA correctly from the outset.
